title: BNCI 2019-001 Motor Imagery dataset for Spinal Cord Injury patients
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 10 patients with spinal cord injury performing five distinct hand and arm motor imagery tasks: hand open, palmar grasp, lateral grasp, pronation, and supination. The study investigates the decoding of attempted movements from low-frequency EEG signals (movement-related cortical potentials) to support neuroprosthetic applications for upper limb control. The dataset includes 360 trials (72 per class) acquired at 256 Hz with 61 EEG channels and 3 EOG channels, along with preprocessing details and classification performance metrics.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired at 256 Hz using 61 active electrodes in a 10-5 montage (g.tec g.GAMMAsys/g.LADYbird cap) with reference at left earlobe and ground at AFF2h. Participants performed five motor imagery tasks cued visually for 3 seconds followed by 3 seconds of imagery execution. Online filters included 50 Hz notch and 0.01-100 Hz bandpass. Preprocessing involved bandpass filtering (0.01-100 Hz, Chebyshev order 8), ICA-based artifact removal, trial rejection based on amplitude (±100 μV) and statistical criteria, and common average re-referencing. Final analysis used 0.3-3 Hz bandpass filtering with shrinkage LDA classification.
